about: What the NFT wave got right, where it broke, and what makes each one real here. Prose only: every number the page shows beside a row is computed from data (world.json, the creatures' sealed record, the sealed trial), and every row's state is read from its doors' cards by deck.mjs realness(). Sources checked to resolve 2026-09-30.

rows.mechanic: A collection with traits and a rarity table
rows.was: Ten thousand characters, each with traits, and a table counting how rare each trait is (CryptoPunks, 2017).
rows.loved: Hunting the rare one, and being able to count exactly how rare it is.
rows.broke: The rarity came from the creator's generation script. Scarcity was manufactured, not earned.
rows.real: Every card's rarity is computed from what GitHub's own runners did to that build. The rarity table counts evidence, and nobody can move a card up it by saying so.

rows.was: Artworks grown from an algorithm and a seed, each one unique (Art Blocks, 2020).
rows.loved: Art nobody drew by hand, different every time, provably from its seed.
rows.broke: The art said nothing about what the token was or did.
rows.real: Each card's sigil is grown from its own evidence: its symmetry and petals from its genes, and its rings from how far its proof got. The art is a reading of the card.

rows.mechanic: The token pointed at the thing
rows.was: An ERC-721 token holds a tokenURI: a link to metadata and media stored somewhere else.
rows.broke: The thing lived on somebody's server or pin. When that stopped, the token pointed at nothing.
rows.real: A FallKard card carries the build itself inside the picture, in declared chunks, sealed by sha256. Every card also prints its seal on its face, so a stripped copy or a screenshot still finds its build in the holder's deck.

rows.mechanic: The mystery egg and the reveal
rows.was: Mint blind, and the contents are revealed later.
rows.broke: The reveal was a switch the creator flipped. You trusted what came out.
rows.real: Your didy hatches from an egg that already works: no model, no key, no account. What it grows into is decided by a bar anyone can re-run.

rows.was: A profile picture from a collection as who you are online (Bored Ape Yacht Club, 2021).
rows.loved: A face, and belonging to something.
rows.broke: The identity was a picture. It could not do anything.
rows.real: Your didy is your character: an agent you assemble out of real tools, bounded by a capability and a budget it cannot cross.

rows.mechanic: A token that owns a wallet
rows.was: Token-bound accounts: every NFT gets its own account that can hold things (ERC-6551, 2023).
rows.loved: A character that carries its own inventory.
rows.broke: The account could hold anything, and nothing bounded what it could do.
rows.real: The wallet: an Ed25519 identity that is a capability plus a budget it cannot cross, with its lineage attached.

rows.was: Two cats breed a third with inherited traits (CryptoKitties, 2017).
rows.broke: A child was a new picture. It was not better at anything.
rows.real: The creatures of kard-evolve breed and are selected on real work: the champion reads damaged cards better than its first generation did, and what it found shipped into the card format. Offspring lets two parents have a child only through a sovereign coupling.

rows.was: Dynamic NFTs: metadata that updates when something happens, fed by an oracle.
rows.loved: A card that grows with you.
rows.broke: Whoever controlled the oracle decided what changed.
rows.real: A card moves when its own evidence moves, rescanned from GitHub and never edited. A didy grows a stage only when a measured bar says the job needs it, and shrinks when a smaller stage will do.

rows.was: Soulbound tokens: badges that cannot be transferred (Buterin, 2022; EIP-5192).
rows.loved: Reputation that stays with the person who earned it.
rows.broke: Most badges proved you turned up, not that you could do anything.
rows.real: You cannot claim a skill here, only demonstrate it, and anyone can re-grade the record.

rows.mechanic: Creator credit that follows the work
rows.was: A standard way for a creator to be credited on every resale (EIP-2981).
rows.loved: Makers credited for as long as the work travels.
rows.broke: In 2023 the largest marketplace made creator fees optional, and the credit went with them.
rows.real: Credit lives inside the thing, not in a marketplace: a child carries both parents' lines, a fork carries its lineage, and every card names who built it. There is nobody in between to drop it.

rows.was: Holder utility: the token unlocks access, a game or a perk.
rows.loved: A thing you own that does something.
rows.broke: The utility was mostly a roadmap.
rows.real: The card is the thing: open it and the build hatches, in a sandbox, in your browser.

rows.was: Card battles and creature fights (Gods Unchained, Axie Infinity).
rows.loved: A reason to build a deck.
rows.broke: The rarer, dearer cards won. Power was bought.
rows.real: In the arena raw model size does not win, as a tested invariant, and a special only lands if its code passed its gate. Size is for work; fights are won by choosing well.

rows.was: Players pooled into guilds, with scholarships lending creatures to players (Axie Infinity).
rows.loved: Teams, and a way in for people who could not afford to start.
rows.broke: Scholarships became rented labour: the guild took a cut of the player's grind.
rows.real: Guilds here are didys teaming up: whoever grew the bigger model runs the heavy part for everyone. A coupling that only takes is classed as dead.

rows.was: One place to find everything and trade it (OpenSea).
rows.broke: A listing meant nothing. Anyone could list anything.
rows.real: Nothing lists without evidence: the store refuses every build nobody has checked.
